days.headline: Budget second reading vote
days.summary: The second reading debate on the 2027 Budget ends with a vote at 6 pm.

items.title: Appropriation Bill 2027: second reading vote
items.what: Final day of the second reading debate; the House votes at 6 pm.

days.headline: Budget debate begins
days.summary: First day of the second reading debate on the 2027 Budget, from 11 am to 6 pm.

items.title: Appropriation Bill 2027: second reading debate
items.what: Debate on the 2027 Budget runs from 11 am to 6 pm.
points: 9.30 am: business under Standing Orders 22(1) to 22(6)
10 am: five oral questions
10.30 am: one question under Standing Order 27(2)
6 pm: adjournment motions

days.headline: Budget Speech: Appropriation Bill
days.summary: The Order Paper lists the Appropriation Bill for second reading at 1.30 pm, ahead of other bills and annual reports.

items.title: Appropriation Bill 2027: second reading
items.what: First item on the Order Paper; the Finance Minister presents the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Bills listed for second reading
items.what: Bills listed on the Order Paper after the Appropriation Bill; they may not be reached.
points: Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs (adjourned debate)
Sri Lanka Cricket
Protection of the State from Terrorism
Prevention of Organised Crimes
Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters
Immigration
Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka

figs.l: government bills listed after the Budget

items.title: Justice sector annual reports for approval
items.what: Annual reports with Auditor-General observations, already considered by a Sectoral Oversight Committee.
points: Superior Courts Complex Board of Management (2022)
National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses (2022, 2023)
Legal Aid Commission (2022, 2023)
Official Languages Commission (2020 to 2023)
National Institute of Language Education and Training (2022, 2023)

days.headline: Five Members' motions passed
days.summary: The House passed five private Members' motions and received Auditor-General reports. It next sits on 12 November at 1.30 pm.

items.title: Five private Members' motions passed
items.what: Motions on Puttalam line trains, road-reserve trees, Colleges of Education, Udawalawe tourism and water hyacinth were passed.
items.next: Votes and debate to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Auditor-General reports tabled
items.what: Installments of Auditor-General reports for 2019, 2022 to 2025 and the 2025 annual report were presented.

items.title: Bill certificate endorsed
items.what: The Speaker announced a certificate endorsed under Article 79; the record does not name the bill.
items.next: Bill name to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Ministers answer questions
items.what: The Labour Minister answered on unemployment and the fuel subsidy; others replied on Maha farmers and the Asian Games.
items.next: Answers to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Adjournment motion: East Container Terminal
items.what: A motion on completion of the East Container Terminal at Colombo Port was proposed at adjournment.

days.headline: Trusts bill passed; Air Force estimate approved
days.summary: The House approved the Trusts (Amendment) Bill and the Air Force supplementary estimate of Rs. 4.26bn. It next sits on 6 November.

items.title: Trusts (Amendment) Bill
items.what: Read a second and third time and certified by the Speaker the same day, as Act No. 28 of 2026.
items.next: Vote and any amendments to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Supplementary Estimate No. 08 (Air Force)
items.what: Extra spending for the Sri Lanka Air Force to set up an unmanned aerial vehicle system.
points: Debate and approval set for 5 Nov
Record lists Head 224, Programme 01
items.next: Vote count to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Committee reports presented
items.what: Reports of the Public Finance Committee and the Governance, Justice and Civil Protection oversight committee were presented.
items.next: Contents to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Auditor-General reports tabled
items.what: Parts of the Auditor-General's reports for 2024 and 2025 were presented.

items.title: Petitions and questions
items.what: Ten petitions went to the Public Petitions Committee; ministers answered questions on the Mannar-Rameswaram ferry and exports.
items.next: Answers to be added from the Hansard

days.headline: Import regulations and supplementary sums approved
days.summary: The House approved the import regulations and two supplementary sums, and received a Public Finance Committee report. It next sits on 5 November.

items.title: Supplementary Estimate No. 07 of 2026
items.what: The House approved supplementary sums under Head 119 and Head 102 (Programme 01 each).
items.next: Ministry names, amounts and vote to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Import regulations, Gazette 2508/27
items.what: The House approved regulations under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act.
items.next: Vote count to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Organised Crimes Bill: court petitions
items.what: The Speaker announced receipt of copies of petitions filed at the Supreme Court against the bill.
items.next: Supreme Court determination to be announced to the House

items.title: Public Finance Committee report
items.what: The Committee on Public Finance report was presented by its Chair, Dr. Harsha de Silva.
items.next: Contents to be added from the Hansard

items.title: Annual reports tabled
items.what: Six annual reports were presented, including the Department of Pensions and Ceylon Petroleum Storage Terminals for 2025.

items.title: Answer on protecting wild elephants
items.what: The Leader of the Opposition's question on wild elephant protection was taken under Standing Order 27(2).
items.next: Answer to be added from the Hansard

days.headline: Black July committee approved; estimates presented
days.summary: The House approved a select committee on Black July and received two supplementary estimates. It next sits on 4 November.

items.title: Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill
items.what: Presented for the Justice Minister and referred to a Sectoral Oversight Committee.
items.next: Second reading listed for 17 November
points: Presented by the Chief Government Whip
Referred to the Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection

items.title: Organised Crimes Bill: court petitions
items.what: The Deputy Speaker announced 20 petitions filed at the Supreme Court against the bill.
items.next: Supreme Court determination to be announced to the House

items.title: Black July select committee
items.what: The House approved a resolution for a select committee on the 1983 Black July incident, its impact and relief.
items.next: Committee members to be named
points: Moved by Thanura Dissanayake, MP
Seconded by Bhagya Sri Herath, MP

items.title: Supplementary Estimates No. 07 and 08
items.what: Two supplementary estimates for 2026 were presented and referred to the Committee on Public Finance.
items.next: Amounts for No. 07 to be added from the 4 November Hansard
points: No. 08 is for the Sri Lanka Air Force
No. 07 approved 4 Nov; No. 08 approved 5 Nov

items.title: Head 240 allocations report, September
items.what: Report on allocations made from the Department of National Budget head, 1 to 30 September 2026.
points: Laid under section 6(1) of Appropriation Act No. 23 of 2025
Expenditure Head 240, development activities programme
items.next: Amounts to be added when published in English

items.title: Import regulations, Gazette 2508/27
items.what: Finance Minister regulations of 1 October laid before the House and referred to the Committee on Public Finance.
points: Made under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act No. 1 of 1969
Motion to approve due 4 November

items.title: Auditor-General reports and annual reports
items.what: Auditor-General reports for 2020 to 2025 and annual reports of ten public bodies were presented.

items.title: Public Security Ordinance order
items.what: A message from the President on a proclamation under the Public Security Ordinance was read.

items.title: Answers on farmers and Development Officers
items.what: The Minister of Public Administration answered two questions on Maha season farmers and Development Officers.

items.title: Adjournment motion: relief for exporters
items.what: Adjournment debate on financial relief for exporters facing global challenges.

items.title: Rice import levy removed, Gazette 2513/02
items.what: The Finance Minister removed the special commodity levy on imported raw and parboiled rice from 3 November.

figs.l: rice tariff codes no longer levied

points: Made under the Special Commodity Levy Act, No. 48 of 2007, section 2
Order signed by the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development on 2 November
Codes covered: 1006.30.19 (raw rice) and 1006.30.29 (parboiled rice)

src.t: Acts, gazettes and circulars, Ministry of Finance

items.title: Drug-law bills certified
items.what: The Speaker certified both Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) bills passed on 22 October.
points: Act No. 26 of 2026: handling and destruction of seized drugs (Bill 79)
Act No. 27 of 2026: methamphetamine, manufacturing and bail (Bill 80)

days.headline: Rabies bill debated; vote later
days.summary: The second reading debate was adjourned without a vote. The House next sits on 3 November.

items.title: Rabies and dog registration bill
items.what: Second reading debated and adjourned to a later date. No vote was taken.

figs.l: maximum fine, e.g. abandoning a dog

items.next: Debate resumes on a date still to be set

items.title: Anti-terrorism bill: another court petition
items.what: The Speaker announced a further petition against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill.
items.next: Court determination

items.title: Public Finance committee report presented
items.what: Presented by Nimal Palihena, Member of the Committee, for its Chair.
points: Annual reports for 2025: Regional Development Bank; Jaya Container Terminals Limited.
Petitions: one from Nilanthi Kottahachchi and two from R.M. Samantha Ranasinghe, referred to the Committee on Public Petitions.

items.title: Poverty programme figures
items.what: The Prajashakthi national poverty eradication programme, from a written answer published on 23 October.
points: Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment Upali Pannilage, answering Ajith Gihan.
Projects started: 15,316 livelihood, 273 education and 136 health.

items.title: Raised: Asian Games, teachers, pasture lands
items.what: Urgent questions, two ministerial replies and an adjournment motion on tourism.
points: K. Kader Masthan: exclusion of Fathima Shafiya from the 20th Asian Games in Japan.
Shanakiyan Rasamanickam: teacher recruitment, and Development Officers not absorbed into the Teachers' Service.
Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation K.D. Lal Kantha: pasture lands in Madavanai, replying to a question of 23 September.
Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government A.H.M.H. Abayarathna: local authorities in the Northern and Eastern Provinces, replying to a question of 25 September.
Nishantha Perera: adjournment motion on Benthara, Karandeniya and Elpitiya as new tourism zones.

days.headline: Two drug-law bills passed
days.summary: Both drug-law amendments passed with changes. Nine annual reports approved, four from 2015 to 2018.

items.title: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Bills
items.what: Bill 79 covers how seized drugs are handled and destroyed. Bill 80 covers methamphetamine, manufacturing and bail.
items.next: Certified 30 Oct as Acts No. 26 and 27 of 2026

items.title: Anti-terrorism bill: more court petitions
items.what: Further petitions against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill.
items.next: Court determination

items.title: Nine annual reports approved
points: Janatha Estates Development Board: 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018
National Institute of Labour Studies: 2022
National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health: 2022
Ranaviru Seva Authority: 2023
Kotelawala Defence University: 2022, 2023

items.title: Committee report and three annual reports tabled
items.what: The Governance, Justice and Civil Protection oversight committee reported.
points: 2024 annual reports: Official Languages Commission; Ceylon German Technical Training Institute; Institute of Human Resource Advancement, University of Colombo.

items.title: Figures given to the House
points: Rabies: Minister of Health and Mass Media Nalinda Jayatissa.
Fences: Minister of Environment Dammika Patabendi.
Pepper: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Namal Karunaratne.

items.title: Answers on reserves and El Niño
items.what: Replies to questions held over from August and September.
points: Official reserves: Anil Jayantha, Minister of Labour and Deputy Minister of Finance, replying to Ravi Karunanayake (asked 18 August).
El Niño and recovery after Cyclone Ditwah: Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekera, replying to Sajith Premadasa.

items.title: Raised: 2026 Budget progress, Middle East conflict
items.what: Urgent questions, and an adjournment motion on a diplomatic reception.
points: Sajith Premadasa: progress of the 2026 Budget proposals.
Ravi Karunanayake: economic impact of the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran.
Dilith Jayaweera: motion on the reception for Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister.

days.headline: Borrowing resolution and extra spending approved
days.summary: Amounts are not in the same-day record. They follow with the Hansard.

items.title: Debt resolution, Public Debt Management Act
items.what: Amount and terms not yet published.

items.what: Extra spending for the Department of Development Finance (Head 243).

items.title: Trusts (Amendment) Bill
items.what: Amends the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87).
items.next: 14 days for court challenges

items.title: Court petitions on three bills
items.what: Sri Lanka Cricket, anti-terrorism and Immigration bills.

items.title: Public finance and debt reports
items.what: Committee on Public Finance report and the debt office's 2025 performance report.
points: Also: the Environment, Agriculture and Resource Sustainability oversight committee report.
Follow-ups to Committee on Public Accounts findings: Ministry of Digital Economy, Ministry of Technology, Western Provincial Council.

points: Sri Lanka Export Development Board: 2021, 2022, 2023
National Gem and Jewellery Authority: 2022, 2023
Gem and Jewellery Research and Training Institute: 2023
National Salt Ltd: 2021/22, 2022/23
BCC Lanka Ltd: 2021/22, 2022/23

items.title: Prison numbers
points: Minister of Justice and National Integration Harshana Nanayakkara.
Largest age group: 30 to 40, with 3,423 prisoners.

items.title: Raised: liquor licences, remembrance day, Sathurukondan inquiry
items.what: Urgent questions and ministerial statements.
points: Shanakiyan Rasamanickam: illegal liquor and new liquor licences.
Ramanathan Archchuna: Thileepan remembrance day.
Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala: the Sathurukondan killings inquiry, and ethnic harmony and national security.

days.headline: Security bills presented; container inquiry extended
days.summary: A customs duty order and seven education orders reached the House, one of them 887 days after it was gazetted.

items.title: Organised Crimes and Foreign Terrorist Fighters bills
items.what: Give effect to a UN convention and UN Security Council Resolution 2178.
items.next: 14 days for court challenges

items.title: Customs import duty order, Gazette 2502/21
items.next: Rates to be added from the Gazette

items.title: Seven higher-education orders
items.what: New private degrees and two name changes.
points: Degrees: SLIIT, Sri Lanka Technology Campus, KIU Campus, The American College of Higher Education, Sri Lanka Institute of Textile and Apparel.
Renamed: SLT Campus; Esoft Metro Campus, now Esoft Uni.

items.title: Court petitions: Cricket and anti-terrorism bills

items.what: Containers released from Colombo Port without the mandatory physical inspection.
points: The select committee was set up by a resolution of 19 November 2025.

items.title: Anti-corruption oversight committee
items.what: Oversees Parliament's part in the National Anti-Corruption Action Plan 2025 to 2029.

items.title: Auditor-General reports and papers
points: Annual reports include Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation and its life and general companies (2025), ITN, the National Transport Commission and the Sri Lanka Cashew Corporation (2024).
Committee on Public Accounts follow-ups: Department for Registration of Persons; local authorities in the Central and Western provinces.

items.title: Statements: power outage, tusker Kavantissa
items.what: The island-wide outage of 17 October, and the death of a tusker.
points: Minister of Energy Anura Karunathilaka, replying to Ravi Karunanayake.
Minister of Environment Dammika Patabendi, replying to Sajith Premadasa.
Adjournment motion on the country's situation: Gayantha Karunathilleka.

items.title: Anti-Corruption (Amendment) certified
items.what: Signed by the Speaker. Printed as Act No. 25 of 2026.

points: Fisheries Corporation report referred to the oversight committee on environment, agriculture and natural resources.
Public petitions referred to the Committee on Public Petitions.

items.title: Employment of persons with disabilities
points: Answer given by the Deputy Minister, Wasantha Piyathissa.
Subsidy covers 50% of salary.

items.title: Regional Development Bank branches and staff
points: Answer given by the Deputy Minister, Nishantha Jayaweera.
Eight provincial offices to merge into four regional offices.

items.what: Second and third readings, without a division.
items.next: Certified 19 October

posts.wa:
2027 Budget presented today; PPP bill published
- Parliament sits at 1.30 pm today for the 2027 Budget Speech on the Appropriation Bill
- Second reading debate runs 13 to 20 November; committee stage 21 November to 14 December
- A Public Private Partnership Bill, published 10 November, would set up a National Agency for Public Private Partnerships
- The Civil Procedure Code (Amendment) Bill had its first reading on 3 November and was referred to a Sectoral Oversight Committee
Next: second reading vote on the Budget at 6 pm on 20 November; final vote at 6 pm on 14 December.
